chunks.content: ## CLO Strap Wearing Techniques: Ring Display and Sewing Methods This document explains detailed procedures for creating and simulating strap wearing effects in CLO 3D, focusing on ring display techniques, panel modeling, sewing methods, and simulation adjustments for realistic strap presentation. Key terms include strap panel, ring plate, folding arrangement, sewing line adjustment, sticky layers, and butterfly knot. --- ### Creating and Positioning the Strap Ring Panel This section covers how to create a ring plate for the strap using CLO’s shape and positioning tools, including hardening, folding, and adjusting the panel to simulate a ring structure. - Start by selecting the strap version and switching the strap type to a harder material to avoid deformation during simulation. - Use the shape tool to create a ring plate of suitable size. - Sew the ring plate onto the back piece of the model. - In the 3D window, add the ring plate to the side and position it near the model using the positioning ball tool. - Add an inner line in the middle of the ring panel to create a fold. - Harden the panel before folding to maintain shape. - Use the folding arrangement tool: set the fold angle to 0°, change the model type to TURN, and sew the fold line. - Reduce particle diameter and gap thickness for this small panel to enhance detail. - Remove hardening after folding and adjust the inner line angle to 180° to round the panel. - Increase folding strength to maintain the 180° fold angle for a more pronounced curve. --- ### Sewing Fixation and Symmetry for Strap Panels This section explains how to fix the strap panel by sewing, creating symmetrical panels, and freezing components to prepare for simulation. - Remove previous sewing lines on the ring panel. - Duplicate the panel symmetrically using the colon symmetrical panel function. - Freeze the back piece and the strap panel to prevent unwanted deformation during simulation. - Activate both straps and sew them onto the pre-made belt panel. - Use the 3D view to verify correct sewing position; adjust as necessary. - Reduce the instance count of panels to 3 for performance optimization. - Add a sticky layer between the two strap boards to prevent deformation during simulation. --- ### Creating and Measuring Additional Belt Strap Boards This section details how to measure and create additional boards for belt straps, including length and width measurements, positioning, and sewing. - Use the measuring tool to measure the length of the new strap section: click once to start and double-click to end measurement. - Length measured was slightly over 127mm; create a board of 130mm in length. - Measure the width of the belt (7.9mm) and create a board with a height of 8mm accordingly. - Position the new board behind the model using the positioning ball and arrow tool for precise placement. - Create instances of the board for left and right sides.

chunks.content: - Use the measuring tool to measure the length of the new strap section: click once to start and double-click to end measurement. - Length measured was slightly over 127mm; create a board of 130mm in length. - Measure the width of the belt (7.9mm) and create a board with a height of 8mm accordingly. - Position the new board behind the model using the positioning ball and arrow tool for precise placement. - Create instances of the board for left and right sides. - Use the plus point division tool to add two straight points in the middle of the board. - Apply left and right symmetry using the adjustment board tool for balanced design. - Sew the boards using 2D and 3D views to ensure correct orientation; use the ice sewing line tool to reverse sewing direction if necessary. --- ### First Wearing Method: Fake Wear with Fixed Sewing Line This section describes the “fake wear” technique where the strap is sewn onto the board but does not simulate real deformation. - Sew the strap panels onto the belt board. - Remove the visual effect of the sewing line by selecting the sewing lines and setting their strength to 0 in the attribute editor. - Adjust the sewing line to the middle position for more realistic appearance, as it is fixed from above. - Add thickness to the sewing line to make it visible on thick texture surfaces. - Shorten the middle rope in the simulation for a more realistic look. - This method offers a stable but non-deformable strap wearing effect. --- ### Second Wearing Method: Real Wear with Dynamic Simulation This section covers the real wear technique, allowing the strap to dynamically simulate passing through the ring. - Delete the fixed sewing line from the fake wear setup. - Hide the fixed board(s) using Shift + Q to work with only the relevant components. - Sew the two strap boards together directly in 3D. - Use Shift + W to show all boards and adjust their position to align in the middle of the ring. - Remove the middle section of the board to facilitate stretching and deformation. - Freeze the back model to avoid unwanted movement. - Simulate the model to verify that the strap passes through the ring naturally. - Use different sticky types to stabilize the strap inside the ring; softer stickies allow flexible but stable positioning. - This method results in a realistic, dynamically deforming strap through the ring structure. --- ### Final Optimization: Sewing Line Effects and Butterfly Knot Addition This section explains final touches for realism, including adjusting sewing line intensity and adding decorative butterfly knots. - Use the edge sewing line tool to reduce hairline intensity of sewing lines for subtle detail. - Add a butterfly knot panel at the end of the strap using the drawing file components.

Both stable (fake wear) and realistic (real wear) methods are demonstrated with detailed instructions on positioning, sewing, hardening, folding, and simulation adjustments to achieve professional strap display results.
